title: Innovation and the performance of informal enterprises in developing countries: a gender perspective
publisher: International Journal of Gender and Entrepreneurship 13(4), 277–301
summary: The study looks at product innovation in informal enterprises to understand how it affects employment in female- and male-owned firms. Product innovation has beneficial effects on job creation, and the authors conclude that innovation is gendered and needs a gendered policy lens.
keyFindings: Product innovation has beneficial effects on job creation in informal enterprises.
There are no systematic differences in the factors affecting product innovation in female- and male-owned enterprises.
Female-owned enterprises are less likely to introduce product innovations, but they sell more innovative products.
methods: Unique data on 513 informal enterprises in Accra and Tema, Ghana, 2013–2015, analysed with a dose-response model.
